patterns.description: Los resultados de ventas documentados por vendedores se separa en polos en el corpus: un polo co-ocurre con cifras de ingresos anuales altos; el polo opuesto co-ocurre con cifras bajas o nulas. La distribución no converge hacia un rango típico.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-050: Seller reported $61,411 in digital product sales in 2025, ranked #238 among all creators
signal_summaries.SC-R1-060: Seller reported nearly $15,000 in sales on Gumroad in 2025
signal_summaries.SC-R1-054: Seller reported $65.15 in 4 hours and described stacking $50-$200 in daily organic revenue
signal_summaries.SC-R1-039: Blog author reported $3,271 in total sales in the first six months
signal_summaries.SC-R1-056: Seller reported making $139.96 total in three years on Gumroad
signal_summaries.SC-R1-051: Seller reported making approximately $21 in total within a week of starting
signal_summaries.SC-R1-049: Seller with 35 product listings reported zero organic traffic

patterns.routing_rationale: The corpus documents seller outcomes at both ends of the distribution: cards in the high-outcome pole (SC-R1-050, SC-R1-060, SC-R1-054) document thousands to tens of thousands of dollars; cards in the low-outcome pole (SC-R1-056, SC-R1-051, SC-R1-049) document under $150 over multiple years or zero traffic with 35 products. Both poles have 3+ cards. The distributional skew is documented, not inferred. Mixed units declared: figures are self-reported seller claims spanning different time periods (1 week to 3 years) and measurement bases (gross revenue, not net). Units are not normalized.

components.label: Polo A: sellers with outcomes in the upper range visible in the corpus
components.summary: Cards documenting high seller outcomes: $61,411 annual, ~$15,000 annual, $65.15 in 4 hours with described daily organic revenue. All are seller self-claims from blog sources.

components.label: Polo B: sellers with outcomes in the lower range or zero visible in the corpus
components.summary: Cards documenting low or zero seller outcomes: $139.96 over 3 years, ~$21 in first week, zero organic traffic with 35 products. All are seller self-claims from blog sources.

patterns.description: Las tarifas aplicadas a ventas en Gumroad se separa en polos según el canal de venta: un polo co-ocurre con tarifas del 10%-10%+$0.50 para ventas web estándar; el polo opuesto co-ocurre con tarifas del 30%-40% para ventas vía Discover web y app móvil. La distribución no converge en una tarifa única.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-005: Pricing page: 10% + $0.50 per transaction for standard sales
signal_summaries.SC-R1-007: Pricing page: no monthly fee, only a percentage of each sale
signal_summaries.SC-R1-032: Help center: 10% flat fee per sale
signal_summaries.SC-R1-035: Help center fees article: 10% flat fee for sales on Gumroad website
signal_summaries.SC-R1-006: Pricing page: 30% fee when new customers find seller through Gumroad Discover marketplace
signal_summaries.SC-R1-036: Fees article: 40% total for mobile app sales (10% Gumroad + 30% App Store/Google Play)
signal_summaries.SC-R1-038: Discover help article: 40% fee for all in-app sales on Gumroad Discover mobile

patterns.routing_rationale: The corpus documents three distinct fee levels for the same platform depending on the sales channel: 10%-10%+$0.50 for standard web sales (4 cards), 30% for Discover-originated web sales (1 card), and 40% for mobile app sales (2 cards). Both poles (low-fee and high-fee channels) have card support. The distributional skew is explicit in official platform documentation. Mixed units declared: SC-R1-005 states percentage + fixed charge while SC-R1-032 and SC-R1-035 state percentage only; SC-R1-036 and SC-R1-038 include third-party store fees in the total. Units are not normalized across cards.

components.label: Polo A: standard web sale fees (10% to 10%+$0.50)
components.summary: Four cards from pricing page and help center document standard web sale fee as 10% or 10%+$0.50 with no monthly fee

components.label: Polo B: Discover and mobile app fees (30%-40%)
components.summary: Three cards document higher fee tiers: 30% for Discover-originated web sales, 40% total for mobile app sales (including Apple/Google store cut)

patterns.description: La disponibilidad de pago para vendedores se distribuye de forma asimétrica en el corpus: las cartas que documentan disponibilidad de pago co-ocurren con cobertura geográfica amplia; las cartas que documentan restricciones de pago se concentran en el caso de países sin depósito directo ni PayPal, con pago imposible.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-027: Help center states 160+ countries can accept payments, with direct deposit or PayPal depending on country
signal_summaries.SC-R1-011: Pricing page states payout method (direct deposit or PayPal) varies by country
signal_summaries.SC-R1-024: Help center: if direct deposit and PayPal both unavailable in seller's country, there is currently no way to pay the seller
signal_summaries.SC-R1-025: Help center: PayPal payouts in USD, 1-3 business days; Payoneer, Wise, check, money order, wire transfer not supported
signal_summaries.SC-R1-028: Help center: if PayPal not supported in seller's country, Gumroad cannot pay them; Payoneer, wire deposits, and bitcoin listed as unavailable

patterns.routing_rationale: The corpus documents an asymmetric payout landscape: two cards document broad geographic availability (160+ countries, two payout methods); three cards document a restricted sub-case where no payout method is available, with an explicit list of unavailable alternatives. Both poles are documented. The skew is explicit: the broad availability claim sits against a documented hard cutoff for a subset of countries. This changes a design decision for sellers in countries without direct deposit or PayPal.

components.label: Polo A: payout available in 160+ countries via direct deposit or PayPal
components.summary: Two cards document that sellers in 160+ countries can receive payouts via direct deposit or PayPal depending on country

components.label: Polo B: no payout available in countries without direct deposit or PayPal
components.summary: Three cards document that sellers in countries lacking both direct deposit and PayPal support have no available payout path; Payoneer, Wise, wire, and bitcoin explicitly listed as unavailable

patterns.description: La cobertura de archivos en Gumroad se separa en polos según el tipo de producto: SC-R1-031 y SC-R1-071 co-ocurren documentando un límite de 250 MB para productos gratuitos versus 16 GB para productos de precio mayor a $0.99. La distribución no converge en un solo límite.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-031: Help center: free products 250 MB limit; products above $0.99 have 16 GB per-file limit with unlimited files; Download all button only shown when total content under 500 MB
signal_summaries.SC-R1-071: Help center: free products 250 MB limit; products above $0.99 have 16 GB per-file limit with unlimited files

patterns.routing_rationale: Two cards document the same file size asymmetry (250 MB free vs 16 GB paid), confirming the asymmetry with consistent data. Both cards are from the same help center source (article 289) and represent the same policy stated twice. The asymmetry is documented but both poles are from the same source. The pattern has 2 cards minimum but they are from the same URL, which reduces independence. The distributional skew (64x difference in file size limit) is documented but the practical friction for free vs paid sellers needs audit to determine if this rises to tension_candidate.

components.label: Polo A: free product file size limit (250 MB)
components.summary: Two cards from the same help center article document that free products are capped at 250 MB file size

components.label: Polo B: paid product file size limit (16 GB per file, unlimited files)
components.summary: Two cards document that products priced above $0.99 allow up to 16 GB per file with unlimited file count

patterns.description: La experiencia de soporte y gestión de cuentas se distribuye de forma asimétrica en el corpus: cartas de documentación oficial co-ocurren con descripciones de procesos definidos; cartas de vendedores se concentran en experiencias de soporte sin resolución y suspensiones sin explicación.

signal_summaries.SC-R1-029: Help center: account suspension for high chargeback rate holds balance 30-45 days before release pending banking partner clearance
signal_summaries.SC-R1-046: Blog post: many Gumroad users faced delayed payouts, poor customer support, and account suspensions without clear reasons; some struggled to get money back
signal_summaries.SC-R1-053: Blog seller: sent multiple emails to Gumroad support over unresolved account verification issue following all available instructions

patterns.routing_rationale: The corpus shows an asymmetry between official policy documentation (SC-R1-029 describes a defined suspension process with specified timelines) and seller experience reports (SC-R1-046, SC-R1-053 describe opaque suspensions, delayed payouts, and unresolved support). Both poles have card support. However, SC-R1-046 is comparative_commentary (not a first-person account) and SC-R1-053 is a single seller's account verification issue. The pattern needs audit to determine whether the documented opposition represents a systemic friction or isolated cases.

components.label: Polo A: official policy describes defined suspension and payout processes
components.summary: Official help center article documents a defined 30-45 day hold process during suspension pending banking partner clearance

components.label: Polo B: seller reports of opaque suspensions and unresolved support
components.summary: Two cards document seller experiences of account suspensions without clear reasons, poor customer support, and unresolved verification issues
